---
title: "1. Python and Computing for Research"
---

::: {.module-meta}
**Duration:** 10 weeks  
**Outcome:** Build a reproducible research-software repository.
:::

## Core topics

Python; NumPy; pandas; Polars; scikit-learn workflow; SQL; Linux shell; Git; testing; packaging; reproducible environments.

## Online courses

- Harvard **CS50P: Introduction to Programming with Python** — <https://cs50.harvard.edu/python/>
- MIT **The Missing Semester of Your CS Education** — <https://missing.csail.mit.edu/>
- MIT **6.100L: Introduction to CS and Programming Using Python** — <https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/6-100l-introduction-to-cs-and-programming-using-python-fall-2022/>

## References

- Python Software Foundation. *The Python Tutorial*. <https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/>
- Chacon, S., & Straub, B. (2014). *Pro Git* (2nd ed.). Apress. <https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2>

## Milestone

Rebuild an empirical project as a tested, documented repository using Git, Python and SQL.

**Next stage**

Recommended bridge: Before Stage 2, complete the Machine Learning Specialization by Andrew Ng or demonstrate equivalent knowledge of supervised learning, regularisation, tree methods, model evaluation and basic unsupervised learning.
